citation.sourceDocument: U.S. Treasury (TreasuryDirect), Series I Savings Bond fixed rate and semiannual inflation rate by rate period (through May 2026)
citation.sourceNote: A Series I savings bond's composite rate is set twice a year, each May 1 and November 1, from two parts: a FIXED rate that is set when you buy and then never changes for the life of that bond, and an INFLATION rate that follows CPI-U and resets every six months for every bond. They do not simply add — the Treasury's formula is fixed + 2×semiannual inflation + (fixed × semiannual inflation) — and the composite rate can never go below zero even when inflation does. This shard is the history of both components, so a bond bought in any period can be valued with the fixed rate it actually carries rather than today's. The rules that shape the answer and are not modeled: a one-year minimum holding period, a three-month interest penalty for redeeming before five years, a $10,000 per person per calendar year electronic purchase limit (plus $5,000 in paper bonds via a tax refund), and interest that is exempt from state and local tax and federally deferrable until redemption — or excludable entirely under the §135 education exclusion if you qualify. Each period's rate applies to a bond starting from ITS OWN six-month anniversary, not from the announcement date, so a bond's rate changes on a schedule set by its purchase month rather than in May and November.
